newsitem.title: USA: Wilshire Tech says not cash flow positive.
newsitem.headline: Wilshire Tech says not cash flow positive.

text.p: Wilshire Technologies Inc said Wednesday that although revenues have increased and operating costs have been reduced in the past year, it is not yet cash flow positive.

Trilon Dominion Partners LLC, the largest shareholder with over 72 percent of the shares outstanding, has continued to provide financial support during 1996 and management believes that support will continue in 1997.
As a result, the company's independent auditors have removed the "going concern" paragraph from their report on the financial statements for the year ended November 30, 1996.

The company said it completed major steps in 1996 to focus on businesses where it has a technological competitive advantage and to structure those businesses for improved profitability. The strategic divestitures of the medical products and transdermal products businesses effectively remove the company from the highly regulated pharmaceutical and medical device industries with their related high research and development costs.
In addition, the relocation of the developmental glove plant from the United Kingdom to Tijuana, Mexico, greatly improves the operating efficiency of that business and significantly reduces costs.

In 1997, the company will focus on expanding its core business of contamination control products used in the clean rooms of electronic component manufacturers and on significantly increasing the production and sales of its proprietary synthetic glove. In contamination control, the company will focus on geographic expansion especially in Southeast Asia, and on new customers for its proprietary swabs and wipes.
In addition, product cost reduction efforts will continue with the transfer of some contamination control production to Mexico.

In gloves, the company will focus on maximizing production from the existing glove manufacturing equipment in Mexico and on completing the purchase and installation of the first full-scale glove production line to increase capacity to over 5 million pairs of gloves per year.

In the fourth quarter ended November 30, 1996, from continuing operations, it reported net sales of $969,000 and a loss of $545,000 or $0.04 a share. For the year ended November 30, 1996, from continuing operations, the company reported net sales of $3,403,000 and a loss of $2,413,000 or $0.20 a share.
All financial results are restated to exclude the results of the Medical Products division which was divested on June 30, 1996, and has been reported as a discontinued operation.

The fourth quarter 1996 loss of $545,000, represented an improvement of $144,000, or 21 percent, from the fourth quarter 1995 loss of $689,000. For the fiscal year of 1996, the loss of $2,413,000 was an improvement of $506,000, or 17 percent, compared to the fiscal year of 1995. The quarter improvements resulted primarily from improved gross profit margins. The fiscal year improvements resulted primarily from reduced interest expense and income from the settlement of a note receivable.
